questions.question: Explain how to decide between perimeter and area for a question, and compute both for the 15 m by 10 m plot, including the fencing adjustment for the 2 m gate.
questions.expected_answer: Edge jobs (fencing, edging) use perimeter; covering jobs (paving, planting) use area. Perimeter: 2 × (15 + 10) = 50 m; fencing needed is 50 − 2 = 48 m because no fence crosses the gate. Area: 15 × 10 = 150 m².

questions.question: For the semicircular bed of radius 3 m (pi = 3,142), find the area and the perimeter, and explain why the perimeter is not simply half the circumference.
questions.expected_answer: Area: half of 3,142 × 3² = half of 28,278 = 14,14 m². Perimeter: half the circumference (9,426 m) plus the straight diameter edge (6 m) = 15,43 m. Cutting the circle creates a new straight edge; perimeter is the complete boundary, so the diameter must be added — area gains no new surface, so it just takes the fraction.

questions.question: Describe the pipeline from 48 m of fencing to a final cost, given 15 m rolls at R520, and justify the rounding direction.
questions.expected_answer: Divide 48 by 15 to get 3,2 rolls; round UP to 4 because 3 rolls (45 m) would leave the fence unfinished — materials buy the smallest whole quantity that completes the job; then 4 × R520 = R2 080.
